subject: Materials Science
title: Titanium: The Implant Metal
description: Learn Titanium: The Implant Metal in one minute.

hook.text: Titanium is lighter than steel, stronger than bone, and the body barely notices it — the perfect implant metal.

buildup.text: A thin TiO₂ oxide layer forms instantly on titanium — this ceramic shell protects it from corrosion.

discovery.text: Bone bonds directly to titanium oxide in a process called osseointegration — discovered by accident in 1952.

twist.text: Brånemark was studying blood flow in rabbit legs — the titanium chambers fused to bone and couldn't be removed.

climax.text: Today, titanium dental implants, hip joints, and spinal cages rely on osseointegration — bone grows into the metal.

punchline.text: An accidental rabbit-leg discovery gave millions new teeth and joints.

quiz.question: What is osseointegration?
options: The process of melting titanium into shape
Bone bonding directly to the titanium oxide surface
Coating titanium with a polymer layer
